about.title: Bell Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Medical malpractice cases are different from most personal injury matters, and that's especially true in California, where a specific statute called MICRA governs how these claims move forward. If you or a family member in Bell believe a misdiagnosis, surgical mistake, medication error, or delayed treatment caused real harm, it helps to understand your case early — before deadlines start working against you. Los Angeles County has numerous hospitals, urgent care centers, and outpatient clinics serving Bell's roughly 36,000 residents, and errors can happen at any of them. Our team reviews the medical record, consults with qualified experts as California law requires, and helps you understand whether what happened meets the legal definition of malpractice — not just a disappointing result.

items.title: Strict, Short Deadlines
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from when you discover the harm, and never more than three years from the injury itself, to bring a malpractice claim. A required 90-day pre-suit notice must go out before a lawsuit is filed, so early action matters.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: Unlike many injury claims, malpractice cases nearly always need a qualified medical expert to establish that the standard of care was breached. Our team can help arrange that review before deciding how to proceed.

items.title: Damages Caps Apply and Change Yearly
items.desc: California law places a cap on non-economic damages in malpractice cases, and that cap rises each year under MICRA. We can explain how the current figure applies to your circumstances.

items.question: How long do I have to file a medical malpractice claim in Bell?
items.answer: Under California's MICRA rules, you generally have one year from when you discovered (or reasonably should have discovered) the injury, but never more than three years from the date of the injury itself. There's also a required 90-day notice period before a lawsuit can be filed. Because these deadlines are unforgiving, it's worth having your situation reviewed sooner rather than later.

items.question: I had a bad medical outcome in Bell — does that automatically mean malpractice happened?
items.answer: No. California law is clear that a poor result alone doesn't establish malpractice; the question is whether a provider's care fell below the accepted medical standard. That's why a qualified medical expert typically needs to review the records. Our team can help arrange that evaluation before any conclusions are drawn.
